headline: AMERICAN EAGLE DRILLS A FULL KILOMETRE FROM SURFACE AT NAK — 1,001m OF 0.46% CuEq, INCLUDING 218m OF 1.01%
snippet: American Eagle Gold Corp. (TSXV: AE) released August 18 results from step-out hole NAK26-87 at its NAK Copper-Gold Project in British Columbia, intersecting 1,001 metres of continuous copper-gold mineralization from surface grading 0.46% CuEq — including a 218-metre high-grade core at 1.01% CuEq — the longest mineralized intercept ever drilled at NAK and among the widest from-surface copper-gold intercepts reported in Canada this year. Three additional western step-out holes (NAK26-84, -86, -88) extended the mineralized footprint north and west, a geometry with favourable implications for open-pit strip ratios and the scale of what is emerging as a large, bulk-tonnage copper-gold system.

headline: GLADIATOR METALS HITS 40m @ 1.98% Cu AT COWLEY YUKON — PROGRAM DOUBLES TO 14,000m, SECOND RIG INBOUND
snippet: Gladiator Metals Corp. (TSXV: GLAD) announced August 19 that drill hole CPG-158 at its Cowley Park Project in the Whitehorse Belt, Yukon, returned 49.0 metres grading 1.72% Cu, 0.27 g/t Au, 11.44 g/t Ag and 800 ppm Mo from 74.0 metres, including a headline 40.0-metre interval at 1.98% Cu and 920 ppm Mo — consistent high-grade copper-molybdenite skarn that is now confirmed across 28 holes and 4,218 metres. The program has expanded from an initial 8,000 metres to more than 14,000 metres, a second drill rig arrives by month-end, and a fully funded >$40 million exploration budget targets >100,000 metres across the Whitehorse Belt in 2026–27.

headline: WELLS FARGO TRIMS GOLD TARGET TO $4,900–$5,100 BUT STAYS BULLISH — FADING RATE HIKE ODDS KEEP 11% UPSIDE IN PLAY
snippet: Wells Fargo Investment Institute revised its year-end 2026 gold forecast on August 18, lowering the target range to $4,900–$5,100 per ounce from the prior $5,300–$5,500 while reiterating a bullish structural stance — the firm's third revision of the year, each prompted by changing Fed rate expectations. With spot gold trading near $4,397, the revised target still implies approximately 11% upside by December, and the firm cited fading rate-hike odds following weak U.S. retail sales, resilient Asian demand, and ongoing central bank accumulation at roughly 60 tonnes per month as the pillars supporting the long-term bull case.

headline: SILVER EASES FROM MULTI-YEAR HIGH AT $65 AS U.S.-IRAN STALEMATE EXTENDS — RETAIL SALES MISS WEAKENS FED HIKE CASE FURTHER
snippet: Silver September futures held in the $65–$66 per ounce range on Tuesday, August 18, as U.S.-Iran diplomatic negotiations stalled following the expiration of a 60-day agreement on Monday — reinjecting geopolitical risk premium at the same time weaker-than-expected U.S. retail sales data reduced the odds of a September Federal Reserve rate hike. BlackRock and J.P. Morgan analysts cited in the report see silver surpassing $80 per ounce by year-end, driven by dual monetary demand and industrial offtake from solar manufacturing, EV components, and AI data center infrastructure — a demand floor that is structurally separate from any near-term geopolitical resolution.

headline: NEOTERREX SIGNS LOI TO EARN 100% OF FURY GOLD'S JAMES BAY CU-AU-AG-W PROJECT — QUÉBEC ASSET CHANGES HANDS
snippet: NeoTerrex Minerals Inc. (TSXV: NTX) announced August 18 that it has entered into a letter of intent with Fury Gold Mines Ltd. (TSX: FURY) to negotiate a definitive option agreement covering up to 100% of Fury's Copper-Gold-Silver-Tungsten Reservoir Project — 116 mineral claims across 6,090 hectares in the Eeyou Istchee (James Bay) region of Québec, approximately 390 km north-northeast of Matagami near established hydroelectric infrastructure. The deal reflects the continued trend of Québec critical mineral properties migrating from senior producers — who are rationalising non-core assets — to smaller explorers with the mandate and capital to drill aggressively.

headline: STORM EXPLORATION GETS DRILL PERMIT FOR GOLD STANDARD VMS TARGET — Q3 PROGRAM SET FOR NORTHWESTERN ONTARIO
snippet: Storm Exploration Inc. (TSXV: STRM) announced August 19 receipt of a drilling permit at its Gold Standard Project in northwestern Ontario, clearing the way for a Q3 2026 drill program targeting a Volcanogenic Massive Sulphide (VMS) horizon — the same geological style that hosts major base metal discoveries across the Superior Province. VMS systems typically carry high-grade lead-zinc-copper-silver-gold mineralization concentrated in discrete lenses, making this first-pass drill a binary event for a junior stock with an identifiable geophysical target and permit in hand.

headline: INTREPID METALS PREPS 10,000m PORPHYRY DRILL AT CORRAL COPPER, ARIZONA — MAJOR DRILLING CONTRACTED FOR SEPTEMBER START
snippet: Intrepid Metals Corp. announced August 19 that Major Drilling Group International has been contracted for a planned 10,000-metre drill program at the Corral Copper Project in Arizona, with approximately 5,000 metres targeting expansion of known near-surface copper-gold-silver mineralization and 5,000 metres dedicated to first-ever porphyry tests at depth — a drill-the-vector approach that could reframe the entire project's scale if a porphyry source is intersected. Drilling is scheduled to begin in early September 2026 within a highly prospective Arizona porphyry belt at a time when copper above $6.60/lb provides strong economic justification for accelerated discovery work.

headline: AMERICAN PACIFIC MINING DRILLS 2,048m AT MADISON COPPER-GOLD, MONTANA — SKARN AND PORPHYRY ASSAYS EXPECTED IN COMING WEEKS
snippet: American Pacific Mining Corp. provided an August 17 Phase I progress update at its Madison Copper-Gold Project near Silver Star, Montana, having completed 2,048 metres of a planned 15,000-metre program — 1,620 metres of core targeting the porphyry core and 428 metres of RC holes testing near-surface skarn and high-grade vein expressions. Assays from completed holes are expected in coming weeks, after which an additional 5,000 metres of Phase I results are scheduled for release — a staged disclosure that could serve as a series of catalysts for a project in Montana's established copper-gold district.

headline: KARUS MINING HITS TARGET HORIZON IN FIRST 3 HOLES AT FG GOLD, BC — 7,500m SHV VEIN PROGRAM BUILDING CONFIDENCE
snippet: Karus Mining Inc. (CSE: KARU) reported August 19 that all three completed holes of its 2026 South Cariboo District program have intersected the targeted structural horizon at the FG Gold Discovery in British Columbia, validating the Sediment-Hosted Vein (SHV) geological model that underpins the high-grade discovery made in 2020–21. The company has completed 2,031 metres of a planned 7,500-metre core drill program aimed at extending and defining two high-grade vein corridors, with assay results pending — the confirmation of the structural target in 100% of early holes is an encouraging geological signal ahead of what could be a meaningful resource-delineation result.

headline: STILL HIGHER GOLD AHEAD — WHY $4,300 IS THE LINE IN THE SAND BEFORE JACKSON HOLE ON AUGUST 28
snippet: Kitco's August 17 technical analysis argues that gold's intermediate bull structure remains intact, with the $4,300 level — serving simultaneously as the 20-day moving average and the critical resistance-turned-support zone tested repeatedly since late June — defining the lower boundary of the current consolidation after gold's nine-day run from $4,072 to $4,475. The piece maps the scenario tree for Fed Chair Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole keynote: a dovish signal validates the market's rate-pause interpretation and likely triggers a break above $4,500, while a hawkish recalibration risks testing $4,200 briefly before the structural debasement and central bank demand thesis reasserts itself on the medium-term chart.
